comments.why_zh: Mickens 关于质疑技术的演讲摘要
comments.text_zh: James Mickens 谈这个话题：[VIDEO] > 有些人进入科技行业，是为了尽快造出更新、更刺激的各类技术。我的主题演讲将狠狠批判这些人，并烧掉重要的职业人脉，很可能逼得我去当修士，或加入其他以苦修为宗旨的组织。在这场演讲中，我将解释为什么无处不在的技术之普及是好事——其逻辑等同于说“金星上无处不在的天气”是好事，也就是说，一点也不好。 > 以机器学习以及硅谷想象力中其他仓促上马的产物作为案例研究，我将解释：如果开发者坚持对自己所做的任何事情都字面意义上地不加质疑（因为哪怕是最短暂的反思都会降低 git commit 的频率），那么计算机安全（以及更广义的伦理计算）就很难实现。到某个时刻，我的麦克风会被掐掉，可能是酒店管理方干的，也可能是我自己掐的，因为麦克风就是技术，而我们需要重新找回那种纯粹的质朴——用羊角号和卷成锥形的纸莎草纸来放大我们的声音。我会解释为什么纸莎草纸锥筒不容易遭受缓冲区溢出攻击，最后我会指出，我的新创业公司 papyr.us 正在寻找有才华的全栈开发者，要求能自如地在算盘或旁边几根树枝上执行计算任务。
comments.text: James Mickens on this topic: [VIDEO] > Some people enter the technology industry to build newer, more exciting kinds of technology as quickly as possible. My keynote will savage these people and will burn important professional bridges, likely forcing me to join a monastery or another penance-focused organization. In my keynote, I will explain why the proliferation of ubiquitous technology is good in the same sense that ubiquitous Venus weather would be good, i.e., not good at all. > Using case studies involving machine learning and other hastily-executed figments of Silicon Valley’s imagination, I will explain why computer security (and larger notions of ethical computing) are difficult to achieve if developers insist on literally not questioning anything that they do since even brief introspection would reduce the frequency of git commits. At some point, my microphone will be cut off, possibly by hotel management, but possibly by myself, because microphones are technology and we need to reclaim the stark purity that emerges from amplifying our voices using rams’ horns and sheets of papyrus rolled into cone shapes. I will explain why papyrus cones are not vulnerable to buffer overflow attacks, and then I will conclude by observing that my new start-up papyr.us is looking for talented full-stack developers who are comfortable executing computational tasks on an abacus or several nearby sticks.

comments.author: bitwize
comments.story_title: Just know stuff. (Or, how to achieve success in a machine learning PhD)
comments.why_zh: 一句关于 ML 实践的有趣台词的出处
comments.text_zh: “东西就是东西，兄弟。”——出自 James Mickens 关于机器学习的一次演讲，[VIDEO] 我能证实，ML 在许多企业里的用法就像摔鸡蛋实验：你打开 Jupyter，载入一些数据，摆弄各种模型，直到找到一个拟合数据的模型，然后用它尝试预测未来数据。如果未来结果与模型相符，恭喜：你的鸡蛋安全了，至少从那个高度摔下来是安全的。
comments.text: "The stuff is what the stuff is, brother." --from a James Mickens talk on machine learning, [VIDEO] Can confirm, the way ML is used in many businesses is like an egg drop: You open up Jupyter, load in some data, and play around with various models until you find one that fits the data, then use it to try to predict future data. If the future results comport with the model, congratulations: your egg is safe, at least for drops of that height.

comments.text_zh:
> 如果它不按我期望的方式工作，那它就应该被禁。嗯，是的，这是非常合理的期望。在大多数领域，当你卖一个不工作的东西，那叫欺诈。但在真正关乎安全的领域，监管是最严格的，比如机械或医药领域。如果一辆车有 1% 的概率爆炸并炸死车内所有人，卖它合法吗？为什么 OpenAI 卖一个聊天机器人，在你问它严肃问题时，它有 1% 的概率让你相信彻头彻尾的胡扯，却是可以的？我认为教育和沟通对社会的福祉至关重要，所以我会对这个领域的公司要求更高的标准。

> 另外，NLP 可以用来保护弱势群体免受网络虐待。自动过滤器不理解讽刺、引用、批评……诚然，这避免了 Scunthorpe 问题，但例如，试图防止种族主义辱骂的自动审核机器人，经常把黑人之间互称 n word 的情况也屏蔽掉，而黑人之间这样互称完全没问题。没有什么能取代审核。

> 它帮助人们找到相关内容（他们喜欢的）。也许吧，但我怀疑。我还没见过我真正喜欢的内容的广告/推荐，也没遇到有过这种体验的人。我只从广告商那里听过这种说法，但也许你的体验比我的好？

> 不要因为公司的坏行为而责怪技术。它们的意图会腐蚀任何可用的技术。说得好！但让事情变得更容……
comments.text: > If it doesn't work as I expect it so it should be banned. Well yes that's a very reasonable expectation. In most fields, when you sell something that doesn't work, it's called fraud. But in fields where it actually matter for safety, regulations are most stringent, such as in mechanics or medicine. If a car had 1% chance of blowing up killing everyone inside, would it be legal to sell it? Why is it ok for OpenAI to sell a chatbot that has 1% chance to convince you of utter bullshit when you ask it a serious question? I believe education and communication to be critical to society's wellbeing, so i would hold companies in this field to greater standards. > Also NLP can be used to protect vulnerable groups from online abuse. Automated filters do not understand sarcasm, quotation, criticism... Sure that avoids the scunthorpe problem, but for example, auto-moderation bots trying to prevent racist abuse often censor black people calling one another the n word, which is completely ok. Nothing can replace moderation. > It helps people find related content (which they enjoy). Maybe, but i doubt it. I've yet to see advertisement/recommendations for content i actually enjoy, or to meet people who have such experiences. I've only ever heard that from advertisers, but maybe you have better experience than i do? > Don't blame technology for the bad actions of companies.
